articles.title: I Play Rocky review – Anthony Ippolito adds knockout sweetness to the story of Stallone’s Hollywood triumph
articles.summary: Portraying the humour, passion and grit that took the actor from bit parts to Oscar glory, this making-of tale is even more mythic than the original movie. For fun, excitement and the transcendental thrill of success, there’s nothing to touch this very enjoyable drama about the making of Sylvester…
body: It is the story of the struggling young Italian-American unknown who’d had some minor acting jobs – including softcore pornography – but wrote a thumpingly good screenplay inspired by the underdog white boxer Chuck Wepner, who briefly knocked Ali down in 1975. With tremendous self-belief, Stallone insisted he play the lead role himself, holding out against vast cash offers to just take the writing credit and let an established star into the ring.

As the man himself, Anthony Ippolito is an eerie likeness of the young Stallone. It’s almost a cine-seance: the same face, the same seductively slurred voice, the same ox-adjacent physique (though not as stacked and defined in 1976 as an unclothed man in a comparable role would need to be now). What is so incredible is that Ippolito is no one-trick pony. In the 2022 Paramount+ miniseries The Offer, about the making of The Godfather, he played the young Al Pacino. That was a stunning likeness, too.

articles.title: Liam Neeson Says There’s ‘Nobody Better Than’ Meryl Streep to Take Over Aslan Role in ‘Narnia,’ but Admits He Didn’t Know About Greta Gerwig’s Movie: ‘This Is News to Me’
articles.summary: Liam Neeson is all for Meryl Streep taking over the role of Aslan in Greta Gerwig’s upcoming “Narnia” movie — even if he’s just learning about it now. Neeson, who voiced the mythical lion in the original “Chronicles of Narnia” film trilogy, admitted he was unaware of the new adaptation in a recent…
body: In Gerwig’s “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew,” Streep is voicing Aslan, who created the world of Narnia and is often seen as an incarnation of Jesus. When ScreenRant broke the news to Neeson that Streep would be playing the role, he responded, “Meryl is playing Jesus Christ? Well, if you’re going to make Christ a lady, nobody better than Meryl.”

Of casting Streep as Aslan, Gerwig told Empire: “I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness. Someone who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight. I wanted someone who was older than 70, so there was a wisdom of experience, but who also had the capacity of fresh wonder, like a child. And also to be one of the greatest actors to ever do it. That list is not a long one.”

She said that David Bowie was a source of inspiration for Aslan’s look — who has multicolored eyes and a red-striped face in this version — as well as the essence of the movie, which she described as “big and transporting” and feeling like a “rock opera.”
“Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew” will open in theaters on Feb. 12, 2027, before streaming on Netflix April 2.

body: A24 financed and will distribute the upcoming film. Frequent Luca Guadagnino collaborator David Kajganich (“Bones and All,” “Suspiria”) penned the screenplay, and producers include Ridley Scott’s Scott Free, Berger’s Nine Hours, Pitt’s Plan B, and Kajganich. Further cast includes Julianne Nicholson, Danny Huston, Camille Cottin, Michael Smiley, and Lara Pulver.

The director also briefly mentioned “The Riders” when speaking about one of his earlier films, the Berlinale breakout “Jack.” Both films have seen Berger work with children, with “Jack” starring then 12-year-old Ivo Pietzcker and “The Riders” starring seven-year-old Coco Greenstone as Pitt’s on-screen daughter.

articles.title: ‘I was given the big picture early’: Rory Kinnear on love, drama – and how his father’s death changed his life
articles.summary: When Kinnear was 10, his beloved father Roy died in an on-set accident. This affected how he now approaches his work as an actor, and also his understanding of life’s most important questions. At first glance, Rory Kinnear is Mr Normal. Bald head, nice face, wholly unremarkable.
body: So here I am in his dressing room at the Theatre Royal Haymarket in London, face to face with the man I’ve just seen on stage, and whose films and TV shows I’ve pored over for the past week, failing to recognise him. For starters, at 6ft, he’s taller than he should be. And more hench. And, actually, hotter.

He laughs, and says he’ll take that. “It’s amazing how many people ask me if I’ve lost weight, and say they thought I’d be smaller. They expect I’ll be just like my dad.” His father, Roy Kinnear, small and squat, was one of the most beloved and talented comic actors of his generation. He died at the age of 54 after being thrown from a horse while filming The Return of the Musketeers in 1988.

articles.title: South International Series Festival Prizes: ’Blindspot Berlin,’ ‘The Oligarch and the Art Dealer’ Win Big
articles.summary: “Blindspot Berlin,” a TIFF standout starring “All Quiet on the Western Front” lead Albrecht Schuch, swept Best Fiction Series, Screenplay and an Audience Award at the 4th edition of Cadiz’s South International Series Festival on Wednesday night.
body: Sold by Beta Film and backed by Germany’s ARD, Europe’s biggest public broadcaster, as well as rbb, NDR, and HR, true-crime thriller “Blindspot Berlin” charts German police efforts to prevent Berlin’s Dec. 19 2016 Christmas market terror attack which killed 13 and injured dozens.Yet their efforts are undermined by the very German institutions meant to support them.

From co-creator, co-writer and director David Nawrath (“Your Honor,” “Atlas”),“Blindspot Berlin” was praised by a SISF jury for its “extraordinary narrative force, an experience of suspense and dramatic tension which traps viewers until the end, even if they knew how things finally played out.”

Part of that tension comes from the rationing of information, the jury observes. It also derives from the constant creation of narrative knots of tension, such as in Episode 1 when Detective Lieutenant Frank Laudlin (Schuch) and Iraq-born rookie police officer Isra Al-Husseini (Bayan Layla, “Elaha”) are racing not to stop a terrorist attack but a German-soil-based recruitment for the Islamic State.

articles.title: ‘Married at First Sight’ U.K. Canceled by Channel 4 Following Sexual Assault Allegations
articles.summary: “Married at First Sight” U.K. has been canceled following allegations of sexual assault on the show, broadcaster Channel 4 confirmed today. Based on an Australian format, the series sees experts match two single strangers who meet for the first time on their wedding day before immediately moving in…
body: Earlier this year a BBC investigation by documentary strand “Panorama” alleged there had been three instances of sexual assault during the U.K. version of the series, which is produced for Channel 4 by production company CPL. One man was subsequently arrested on suspicion of rape. All the men accused have denied the allegations.

Season 6, which has already been filmed, will not be broadcast and the spin-off series “Second Married at First Sight,” which was in pre-production when the allegations broke with casting due to take place over the summer, has also been canceled. Previous seasons of the show have since been removed from Channel 4’s streaming platforms although international versions are still available.

Following the investigation, Channel 4 commissioned two separate reviews, which have now concluded. The first, by law firm Clyde & Co, examined whether welfare protocols sufficiently fulfilled Channel 4’s duty of care obligations as set out by media regulator Ofcom. The second review was conducted by former BBC One controller Lorraine Heggessey to determine whether changes to the show would “strengthen contributor welfare.”

articles.title: Jimmy review – simple-minded James Stewart biopic is too straightforward
articles.summary: Riverdale’s KJ Apa gives surprisingly solid performance but this corny look at iconic actor’s life is missed opportunity. The last time New Zealand actor KJ Apa took on a midcentury American pop-cultural icon, he was playing a nominally sexy yet often weirdly bloodless version of Archie Andrews…
body: Stewart insists on serving his country anyway, becoming a bomber pilot and a captain, in command of a squadron whose mission commitments are bumped up as the war proceeds. This means that Stewart keeps losing more of his men, about which he feels enormously guilty. Though he takes some respite in the company of the Englishwoman Lady Julia (Kara Killmer), he clearly suffers from PTSD, which continues well after the conflict as he returns to Hollywood and his pal Frank Capra (Max Casella) convinces him to make It’s a Wonderful Life, the focus for the film’s final stretch.

In this movie’s telling, Stewart’s art feels secondary to him exorcising his wartime demons. It makes sense that Burns and screenwriter Justin Strawhand wanted to choose a smaller portion of the star’s life to convert into a narrative arc. Yet they haven’t avoided the juddery suddenness of a cradle-to-the-grave biopic – the portrayal of Stewart’s lifelong spouse is particularly cursory – before cramming what they have selected into a vaguely faith-based (and tacitly pro-war) framework. Despite Apa’s surprisingly surehanded evocation of the man in question, Jimmy falls somewhere between cosplay and stolen valor.

articles.title: The Pitt and ER are similar enough for lawsuit to proceed, judge rules
articles.summary: The widow of ER creator Michael Crichton argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the 1990s series.
body: US drama The Pitt is similar enough to medical series ER for a lawsuit against its producers to progress, a court in the US has ruled.
The widow of Michael Crichton, who created ER, argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the series, which has been made without proper permission or credit.

A three-judge panel said there are "clear and numerous similarities between The Pitt and ER," which means the case can go ahead. Warner Bros previously described the lawsuit as "baseless" and sought to have it dismissed.

Listing the similarities between the two shows, the court cited the emergency room setting, the fast pace, use of medical jargon, graphic depictions of injuries, and younger doctors fresh from medical school being trained.
points: The widow of ER creator Michael Crichton argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the 1990s series.

articles.title: Married at First Sight UK cancelled after BBC revealed rape allegations
articles.summary: Channel 4 will reinvest the show's budget in "distinctive new programming" and said sorry again to the women involved.
body: Married at First Sight UK will not return, Channel 4 has said, following a BBC Panorama investigation into the hit reality TV show.

The show's budget will be reinvested in "distinctive new programming", the broadcaster's chief executive Priya Dogra said on Thursday, and she repeated her apology to the women involved in the investigation, for the "distress they have clearly felt".

The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis earlier this year, after a Panorama programme which revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show, while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.
A review was commissioned by Channel 4 shortly after the BBC first contacted the broadcaster, with details of the allegations we had heard.
points: Channel 4 will reinvest the show's budget in "distinctive new programming" and said sorry again to the women involved.

articles.title: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
articles.summary: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.
body: India's most expensive film - a lavish retelling of the Hindu epic Ramayana, made in two parts for a reported $500m (£370m) - has opened in cinemas worldwide, sparking enormous expectations and mixed reviews.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience.

One of Hinduism's foundational epics, the Ramayana has travelled across centuries and continents, finding expression in poetry, temple sculpture, shadow puppetry, folk theatre and stories passed down through generations. It has outlasted kingdoms and empires, inspired religious devotion and political movements, and found new life, again and again, on TV and in cinema.
Tiwari's version returns to the familiar story of love, duty, exile and war, set in a world of gods and demons, celestial weapons and mighty kingdoms.
